data.body: RP-01 cache-impact validation completed with live direct-Anthropic and Bedrock calls; no credential values were printed or persisted. Artifact: .joe-janitor/rp01-cache-live-probe.py; detailed table and analysis: .joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-research.md. Models: Anthropic claude-sonnet-4-6 and Bedrock us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6. Both providers returned identical cache/input counts. Current fresh-run agentic reask: retry cache read/write 2,384/1,821; aggregate input/read/write 8,133/2,384/5,743. Proposed same-run Pydantic retry with agentic cache settings: retry read/write 3,920/289; aggregate 8,135/3,920/4,209. Thus the retry read 1,536 more cached tokens (+64%) and wrote 1,532 fewer (-84%). ProcessHistory reduced a synthetic 5,000-character faulty assistant response to 2,013 characters; the retry still read all 3,920 tokens written by request one, proving that truncation after the prior user boundary did not invalidate the cached prefix. A Rebar-owned ModelRetry error was 63 characters; both assistant history and error text must remain bounded. On the single_turn settings arm, same-run retry read only the 2,448-token static system/schema span versus 2,384 for the fresh shape; there was no message-tail benefit. Design implication for pending D2: if same-run retries are approved, every retry-capable structured run must request Rebar existing provider-specific message-tail breakpoint even when outer execution_mode is single_turn. Cache reuse improves billed cache mix/latency but does not shrink context-window use; preserve limits and add long tool-history probes. No production code changed.
